chunks: One of our companions wrote to Abū Ibrāhīm عليه السلام:

Regarding a man who entered Masjid al-Shajarah, performed salat (prayer), and entered ihram. Then he left the mosque, and before reciting the talbiyah, it occurred to him: may he undo that by having intercourse with women?
So he عليه السلام wrote: "Yes," or, "There is no harm in it."

key_terms.بِمُوَاقَعَةِ النِّسَاءِ: by engaging in intercourse with women
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no harm in it
key_terms.مَسْجِدَ الشَّجَرَةِ: Masjid al-Shajarah, a miqat location for entering ihram
key_terms.وَأَحْرَمَ: he entered the state of ihram

ai.seo_question: Can a person nullify ihram before reciting the talbiyah?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a legal ruling concerning ihram before the talbiyah is recited. It indicates that if a person entered ihram at Masjid al-Shajarah but had not yet recited the talbiyah, he could undo that state, and there was no harm in doing so through intercourse.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2569 - One of our companions wrote to Abu Ibrahim (as)

regarding a man who entered Masjid al-Shajarah, prayed, and entered Ihram. Then, before reciting the Talbiyah, he left the mosque and decided to nullify his Ihram by engaging in intercourse with women.
Imam (as) wrote in reply: "Yes" or "There is no harm in it."
